approach.method_basis: The Parent makes local graph edits from one scored current molecule, sanitizes and normalizes each identity, rejects duplicates and directly evaluates the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening score and separately retains its best observation. Ring closure samples hydrogen-bearing attachment pairs within the existing graph-distance range and adds a bond; it can connect sites across already extensive ring frameworks. Same-transition bidirectional tabu matching, the repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle remain in place.
approach.novelty: Add one topology gate specifically to new ring closures. A proposed closure may form a cycle whose chosen existing shortest path contains no old ring atom, one old ring atom, or two adjacent old ring atoms joined by an existing ring bond. These cases retain access to separate, spiro-like and single-edge fused additions while excluding more extensive overlap under this narrow rule. All edit sampling stays unchanged; an otherwise valid fresh rejected closure is replaced by continued sampling from the same source. This differs from the earlier sulfur filter, branch-removal menu and configuration assignment, and incorporates none of them.

hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel close_ring neighbor before tabu testing unless its source shortest path overlaps the existing ring graph in zero atoms, one atom, or exactly one existing ring edge, thereby redirecting new-cycle proposals away from extended or separated ring overlap while retaining the Parent's edit sampling and accepted-score walk.

finding_summary.headline: Targeted ring closures disappear, while the mean score falls by 0.003396
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes that a narrow source-path rule can strongly control ring-junction growth without disabling all closures or disturbing identity, memory and feedback. Most evaluated rings remain, and the admitted closure repertoire still produces improvements. The score cost is nevertheless real on this panel: the parent had 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures in the now-excluded class. Those historical observations explain why score retention required a test, but they do not provide scores for the newly rejected structures or identify which missing transition caused a later loss.

The chemical assessment shows what the topology restriction leaves unresolved. Less elaborate ring cages still contain unusual sulfur coordination, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unspecified configurations. The permitted classes do not establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility, and the rule neither removes complexity already present in a source nor constrains other edit types. The campaign now has evidence that extensive ring overlap can be suppressed selectively, alongside evidence that this degree of suppression did not retain the registered mean-score margin. Ring topology and local chemical bonding remain separate limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 275 valid, fresh ring-closure attempts. Independent reconstruction of the current tabu table shows that 257 of these would otherwise have been admitted; each was replaced by a different neighbor from the same scored source before feedback. Emitted closures with extended or separated overlap fell from 241 to zero. Ring growth remained active through 40 permitted closures: six paths outside existing rings, three with a single old ring atom and 31 sharing one old ring edge. Nine permitted closures beat their source score and seven improved the best archive.

The overall molecules also lost much of the targeted complexity. Among 4,350 emitted neighbors, the number with a pair of RDKit-perceived rings sharing at least three atoms fell from 1,867 to 10, while mean ring-atom participation changed only from 62.89% to 61.70%. This preserved substantial ring content while removing most extensive ring overlap. All batches completed, requiring 12.83 attempts per ten submitted molecules versus 12.15 for the parent. The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.517522, a paired change of -0.003396 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.004044, -0.024305 and +0.010073. DRD2 improved on average; the other four task means declined.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine frameworks retain reactive halogens, unusual sulfur bonding and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The current output remains entirely ring-bearing by the digest's string counter, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.6 to 73.2. Molecules range from compact fused heterocycles to bulky aryl amines and expanded carbonyl-containing heterocycles. The leading structures generally have fewer elaborate cage connections than several parent families, but that does not make their bonding uniformly conventional. Ordinary thioethers, sulfoxides, amides and amines coexist with substituted S-H centres, multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents, N-halogen groups, O-F groups and reactive sulfur-halogen connections. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish neutral solution species for the amines, and the many potentially stereogenic ring and sulfur centres remain unspecified. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and families, with the displayed leaders often concentrated in one closely related series. Synthetic plausibility and drug-likeness are limited primarily by unusual local bonding and reactive functionality, rather than by a lack of rings or heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are compact fused furan/unsaturated sulfur-ring systems bearing an aryl amide or pyridyl ketone. Alkyl, aminomethyl, imine and chlorinated amino substituents decorate the larger ring; the main ring sulfur itself is an ordinary divalent sulfide. The best molecule contains both an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro amide. A close-scoring pyridyl-ketone relative has methylamino and imine groups without an N-halogen bond. Seed 1 retains a comparatively straightforward ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The low examples disrupt the attached aromatic ring, expand or open a heterocycle, or replace the compact carbonyl-containing connection with a more flexible heteroatom chain.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-chloro amines and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
Some alternatives contain labile imines, free thiols, sulfur-halogen groups or cumulated unsaturation.
Partly saturated fused rings and multiple unsaturated connections are not accompanied by defined stereochemistry or alkene geometry.
missing_features: The lowest ring-expanded and chain-like derivatives lack the intact aromatic carbonyl organization present in the stronger structures.

The high-scoring set lacks a systematic series that preserves the fused aromatic carbonyl framework while replacing reactive N-chloro and amino-chloromethyl groups with stable alternatives; a chlorine-free relative already shows that such chemistry can score closely.
Ring substituents with possible stereogenic relationships remain unassigned, and no configuration preference can be inferred from these strings.

The ordinary indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. Thus the observed high-scoring family does not require every reactive chlorine substituent. The gradient favors retention of a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement more clearly than sulfur enrichment. per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are bulky aryl-rich amines built around a saturated diaza ring with N-propyl and N-methyl substituents. A phenyl-pyridyl group and a chlorophenyl group provide aromatic surface, while a small saturated sulfur ring and an S-S connection link the latter to the amine framework. method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

molecular_assessment.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine frameworks retain reactive halogens, unusual sulfur bonding and undefined stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The current output remains entirely ring-bearing by the digest's string counter, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.6 to 73.2. Molecules range from compact fused heterocycles to bulky aryl amines and expanded carbonyl-containing heterocycles. The leading structures generally have fewer elaborate cage connections than several parent families, but that does not make their bonding uniformly conventional. Ordinary thioethers, sulfoxides, amides and amines coexist with substituted S-H centres, multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents, N-halogen groups, O-F groups and reactive sulfur-halogen connections. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish neutral solution species for the amines, and the many potentially stereogenic ring and sulfur centres remain unspecified. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and families, with the displayed leaders often concentrated in one closely related series. Synthetic plausibility and drug-likeness are limited primarily by unusual local bonding and reactive functionality, rather than by a lack of rings or heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are compact fused furan/unsaturated sulfur-ring systems bearing an aryl amide or pyridyl ketone. Alkyl, aminomethyl, imine and chlorinated amino substituents decorate the larger ring; the main ring sulfur itself is an ordinary divalent sulfide. The best molecule contains both an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro amide. A close-scoring pyridyl-ketone relative has methylamino and imine groups without an N-halogen bond. Seed 1 retains a comparatively straightforward ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The low examples disrupt the attached aromatic ring, expand or open a heterocycle, or replace the compact carbonyl-containing connection with a more flexible heteroatom chain.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-chloro amines and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
Some alternatives contain labile imines, free thiols, sulfur-halogen groups or cumulated unsaturation.
Partly saturated fused rings and multiple unsaturated connections are not accompanied by defined stereochemistry or alkene geometry.
missing_features: The lowest ring-expanded and chain-like derivatives lack the intact aromatic carbonyl organization present in the stronger structures.

The high-scoring set lacks a systematic series that preserves the fused aromatic carbonyl framework while replacing reactive N-chloro and amino-chloromethyl groups with stable alternatives; a chlorine-free relative already shows that such chemistry can score closely.
Ring substituents with possible stereogenic relationships remain unassigned, and no configuration preference can be inferred from these strings.

A compact aryl-amide example scores 0.3957609793331631, while replacing its attached aromatic nitrogen-containing ring by an expanded unsaturated ring gives 0.01654726774958358.
